THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is by the Insurance Company, aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 15.03.2018 passed in MVC No.488/2015 by the I Addl. Senior Civil Judge and Member, MACT, Kalaburagi,
('Tribunal'), by which, the Tribunal while partly allowing the claim petition has NC:
2023:KHC-K:8641 awarded compensation of Rs.4,46,000/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.

2. Brief facts of the case are that:
a) on 20.12.2014, appellant while working as a Cleaner in TATA ACE goods vehicle bearing registration No.KA-32/B-3677 which was proceeding from Farthabad to Sindhanoor, met with an accident at 6:00 a.m., near Madbull Canal on Gulbarga-Shahabad Road due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the said The Divisional Manager, National vs Prakash And Anr on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158955789/
2 vehicle, in which, the claimant sustained grievous injuries in the nature of comminuted fracture of clavicle, fracture of scapula, left both bone forearm fracture and injuries on other part of the body.
He was taken to United Hospital for treatment, where he was given treatment as inpatient from 20.12.2014 to 25.12.2014.

Thereafter he was shifted to Ashwin Hospital, Solapur for further treatment where he was inpatient from 25.12.2014 to 10.01.2015 and thereafter he was admitted to NIMS Hospital, Hyderabad between 10.01.2015 to 23.01.2015.

A NC: 2023:KHC-K:8641 complaint was filed in Crime No.113/2014, charge-sheet has been filed against the driver of TATA ACE vehicle, thereupon, a claim petition was filed under Section 166 of MV Act claiming compensation in a sum of Rs.25,75,000/-.
b) Upon service of notice respondent - owner of offending vehicle did not appear and was placed ex-parte.

c) Appellant - Insurance Company appeared, filed statement of objections denying the petition averments, date and place, manner of accident and age and occupation of the claimant and also denied the injuries sustained claimed to have been stated by the claimant.
It is also contended that the driver of the vehicle did not possess valid license and there was breach of terms of the policy.

It was also contended that the claimant was never engaged as a Cleaner in the said vehicle and that he was traveling as unauthorized person in the goods vehicle, as such, sought for dismissal of the claim petition exonerating the Insurance Company.
NC: 2023:KHC-K:8641 d) The Tribunal based on the pleadings, framed issues and recorded evidence.
Appellant-claimant examined himself as PW1 and one Dr. Ramakant Kulkarni, Orthopedic Surgeon was examined as PW2 and exhibited 22 documents as Exs.P1 to P22.
While one Sri Anilkumar, Assistant Manager of Insurance Company has been examined as RW1 and marked 2 documents as Exs.R1 and R2.

e) On appreciation of the pleadings and evidence, the Tribunal held that the accident is on account of rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle, resulting in injuries to the appellant who was working as a Cleaner in the offending vehicle and consequently held that appellant is entitled for the compensation of Rs.4,46,000/-.
Being aggrieved by the same, Insurance Company is before this Court.

3. Smt. Preeti Patil Melkundi, learned counsel appearing for the appellant-Insurance Company reiterating NC: 2023:KHC-K:8641 the grounds urged in the memorandum of appeal vehemently submits that the entire case is based on false and fictitious material, in that she submits though the accident alleged to have been occurred on 20.12.2014 at 6 a.m., the complaint has been filed after two days i.e., on 22.12.2014 at 5.30 p.m.
The reasons for delay in filing the complaint are not acceptable, as the medical records, more particularly, the Wound Certificate did not disclose that the appellant was not in a position to talk.

She further submits that in the complaint for the first time it is mentioned as the claimant was working as a Cleaner in the offending vehicle, however, in the The Divisional Manager, National vs Prakash And Anr on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158955789/
3 charge-sheet the police after investigation have recorded that the claimant was traveling in the goods vehicle.

sentences.text: She also refers to the statement of claimant produced at Ex.R2, wherein the claimant has stated that he went along with Basanna from Gulbarga to Sindhanoor as he had take the TATA ACE goods vehicle for hire purpose.
Thus referring to the aforesaid material evidence learned counsel submits that the entire case is fabricated only to make false claim of NC: 2023:KHC-K:8641 compensation.

She further submits that even if the contents of Charge-sheet is taken into consideration, at the most the claimant may have to be considered as an unauthorized passenger and no liability can be fastened on the appellant, hence, seeks for allowing of the appeal.
4. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent- claimant justifying the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal submits that there is no inordinate delay in filing the complaint.
He submits that considering the nature of injuries sustained by the injured-claimant it cannot be expected for him to have filed the complaint.

Referring to the medical records, namely, Ex.P9 - Treatment Summery submits that the said document reveals the date of admission and date of discharge from United Hospital, wherein, the history of road traffic accident near Shahapur on 20.12.2014 resulting in the injuries sustained by the claimant has been specifically mentioned.

Therefore, he submits that the grounds urged by the appellant even before the Tribunal has been appropriately adverted to NC:
2023:KHC-K:8641 warranting no interference, hence, prays for dismissal of the appeal.

5. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the records.
6.

Though there is a delay in filing the complaint, in the facts and situation in the matter, more particularly, the nature of injuries sustained by the claimant, it cannot be said that the claimant was expected to file the complaint forthwith.
Besides, perusal of Ex.P9 - Treatment summery reveals the claimant was admitted to the hospital on 20.12.2014 and was discharged on 25.01.2014.

The diagnosis referred to therein is gross contamination of left shoulder wound with compound fracture,
left clavicle and scapula left both forearm fracture.

The said document under the heading course in the hospital reads as under:
"Diagnosis: Gross contamination of left shoulder wound with compound fracture, left clavicle and scapula left both bone forearm fracture NC: 2023:KHC-K:8641 Procedure: Wound debridement + dressing Done on 20-12-2014 Course in the Hospital:
Patient presented with A/H/O/RTA near Shahapur B-gudi on 20- 12-2014.
Sustained injury to chest and left shoulders, Deep lacerated wound with contamination along with skin loss on left chest region and left shoulder.
No H/O LOC, vomiting, convulsion, ENT bleed.
Relevant investigations were done.
General surgeon, Pulmonologist, Plastic surgeon, OMF Surgeon opinion taken.
Patient underwent above procedure on 20-12-2017.
Patient was advised through wound debridement + bony stabilization of left clavicle and shoulder girdle patient attenders refused and were Discharged against medical advice.
CT Scan Reports 21-12-2014:

7. Perusal of the said document would reveal the seriousness and extent of injuries suffered by the claimant.
The said document also reveals that the claimant was presented in the hospital with the history of road traffic accident near Shahapur B-Gudi on 20.12.2014.
Besides, the said document at Ex.P9 also refers to reports of MLC.
It may be too much to expect either the claimant himself or attendant of the claimant to have gone and given a complaint personally.

In that view of the matter delay 2 days in filing the complaint cannot be taken to the extent discrediting the entire case of the claimant, with The Divisional Manager, National vs Prakash And Anr on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158955789/
5 - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:8641 regard to occurrence of accident involving the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: As regards the dispute raised by the appellant - Insurance Company of nature of avocation being carried out by the claimant i.e., as a Cleaner in the offending vehicle, it is not uncommon that a person is hired in goods vehicle temporarily, even for a limited purpose of one or two trips.

The statement of claimant at Ex.R2 referred to by the learned counsel for appellant-Insurance Company would reveal that on 19.12.2014 at evening the driver of the offending vehicle had taken the injured-claimant along with him to Sindhanoor as the TATA ACE was hired to carry the goods from Asian Pain Godown.

Though, learned counsel for the appellant pointed out that in the complaint the description of avocation of the injured is shown as Cleaner, in the charge-sheet it is shown as Coolie and in Ex.R2 it reveals that he has merely accompanied the driver of the offending vehicle.

A holistic reading of these three statements would reveal that the claimant had gone - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:8641 in the goods vehicle at least as a labourer, which can be termed as a Coolie or a Cleaner, as the case may be.
That apart in the charge-sheet it is also clear that along with the driver of the vehicle claimant was the only person who was traveling in the vehicle.
Overall material and circumstances of the matter would lead to a presumption that he was engaged by the driver of the vehicle to assist him in carrying the load from Gulbarga to Sindhanoor.

Though all possible grounds have been raised by the appellant-Insurance Company to discredit the case of the respondent-claimant with regard to the very accident and the nature of his avocation, the said grounds have not been substantiated by leading any cogent evidence to accept the contention of the breach of terms of the policy.
The Tribunal having dealt with these aspects of the matter has partly allowed the claim petition, which in the considered view of this Court does not warrant any interference.
As such, the appeal is dismissed.
The amount in deposit be transmitted along with TCR to the Tribunal.

Sd/-
